belief: My needs and feelings never count.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that your needs and feelings never count, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching about self-denial that left no room for your own needs. A home where your feelings were ignored, dismissed, or punished. Being the caretaker in a struggling family. Hearing “JOY means Jesus first, Others second, Yourself last” as “yourself never.” Fear that having needs is selfish.
teaches: Jesus calls us to deny ourselves and love others, but He never taught that our needs and feelings do not matter. He told us to love our neighbor as ourselves. Paul said to look not only to your own interests but also to the interests of others, which assumes your own interests count too. God knows you completely, cares for you, and invites you to cast all your anxiety on Him. Jesus Himself rested, ate, wept, and asked His friends to stay with Him.
self_statements: It’s selfish to want anything for myself.
I shouldn’t bother anyone with how I feel.
If I have needs, I’m being weak.
God doesn’t care about my feelings.
errors: Treating your needs as less real than everyone else’s.
Believing you must either ignore yourself or be selfish.
Assuming others will see your needs as a burden.
questions: What does “love your neighbor as yourself” assume about my own needs?
Does Philippians 2:4 say to ignore my interests completely?
Did Jesus have needs and feelings?
Who taught me that my feelings don’t count?
Can I care for others better if I never care for myself?
What does 1 Peter 5:7 say God does with my worries?
What is one need I have been ignoring?
truth: My needs and feelings count. God knows me fully and cares for me. Jesus Himself had needs and feelings. I can love others and also take reasonable care of myself. I can share my needs, ask for help, and cast all my anxiety on God, because He cares for me.
hw_questions: What does “as yourself” assume about my needs?
Does Paul say to ignore my interests completely?
Did Jesus have needs and feelings?
Who taught me my feelings don’t count?
Can I care for others well if I never care for myself?
What need have I been ignoring?
hw_truths: My needs and feelings matter to God.
I can love others and take care of myself.
It is not selfish to have needs.
Others can carry my burdens too.
log: Each day, name one thing I felt and one thing I needed, and one small way I honored it.
name_example: Sarah can cast all her anxiety on Him, because He cares for her.
actions: Tell one trusted person how you really feel
Ask for help with one task this week,
Do one thing to meet a real need,
such as sleep, a meal, or quiet time, without apologizing.
Write a list of needs you’ve ignored,
and pray over it, asking God to help you care for yourself wisely.
prayer: Father, thank You that You know me fully and care for me. Help me reject the lie that my needs and feelings never count. Teach me to love others well and to care for myself wisely. Help me bring my needs to You and to others without shame. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
songs: Honesty about struggles makes room for grace and support instead of pretending to be fine.
God’s companionship remains through darkness, weakness, and uncertainty.
God’s fatherly love is deeper than human approval or achievement.
This familiar hymn places confidence in Jesus’ love rather than personal strength.
